## Raw data description

### Raw 16S data

Overall, 166 FASTQ files were received, including forward and reverse reads of 185 samples.  

The 16S region amplified is the V3-V4, using primers:  
Forward: CCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG  
Reverse: GACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC  

The reads are paired-end, 250 nt in each direction.

## Raw data quality

### Read quality

The following plots show the distribution of read quality at each position along the read. As a rule of thumb, quality scores over 30 (red dashed line) are considered good.  

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4, fig.align="center", message=FALSE}
fwd_quality <- read_delim("qiime/combined/1_Import/forward-seven-number-summaries.tsv", 
                          delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE, 
                          escape_double = FALSE, trim_ws = TRUE)
rev_quality <- read_delim("qiime/combined/1_Import/reverse-seven-number-summaries.tsv", 
                          delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE, 
                          escape_double = FALSE, trim_ws = TRUE)

plot_quality <- function(df, direction = 'Forward', vlines = c()){
  # Reorganize table
  df <- df %>%
    filter(...1 != 'count') %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames('...1') %>%
    t() %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column('Position') %>%
    rename_with(function(colname) gsub('%','_quantile',colname)) %>%
    mutate(Position = as.numeric(Position))
  
  ggp<- ggplot(df, aes(x = Position, group = Position)) +
        geom_boxplot(aes(ymin = `9_quantile`, 
                         lower = `25_quantile`, 
                         middle = `50_quantile`, 
                         upper = `75_quantile`, 
                         ymax = `91_quantile`),
                     stat = "identity", fill = 'cadetblue3', color = 'grey30') +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 30, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'darkred') +
        theme_classic() +
        ggtitle(paste('Quality plot -', direction, 'reads')) +
        ylim(c(0,40)) +
        ylab('Quality score') +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  for (vline in vlines) {
    ggp <- ggp + geom_vline(xintercept = vline, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'black') 
  }
  plot(ggp)
}

plot_quality(fwd_quality, vline = c(20,165))
plot_quality(rev_quality, direction = 'Reverse')
```

## DADA2 denoising

[DADA2 algorithm](https://benjjneb.github.io/dada2/index.html) was used for the denoising of raw reads. The DADA2 pipeline specifically includes the following steps:  

* Trimming and quality filtering  
* Learning error models and finding unique amplicon sequence variants (ASV's)  
* Merging paired reads  
* Removing chimeras

DADA2 processing was performed using the qiime plugin, with the following non-default parameters:  

| Parameter            | Description                                             |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
|`DADA_TRIM_LEFT_F=15` | Forward read - left trimming                            |
|`DADA_TRUNC_LEN_F=165`| Forward read - truncation length (0 means no truncation)|  
|`DADA_TRIM_LEFT_R=0`  | Reverse read - left trimming (not used)                 |  
|`DADA_TRUNC_LEN_R=0`  | Reverse read - truncation length (not used)             |  
|`DADA_MAX_EE_F=3`		 | Controls the quality filtering done by DADA. Default: 2 |
|`DADA_MAX_EE_R=4`		 | Same as above, for reverse reads                        |
|`DADA_POOLING=pseudo` | [Pool samples](https://benjjneb.github.io/dada2/pseudo.html#Pseudo-pooling) to identify variants more sensitively. |  


The following plot provides an overview of the number of reads discarded at each step.  
```{r fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3, fig.align="center"}
samples.to.exclude <- c()
pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.4)

ggplot(dada_stats %>% filter(! `sample-id` %in% samples.to.exclude), 
       aes(x = Step, y = Count, fill = Step)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = 'black', width = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(aes(group = `sample-id`), alpha = 0.4, position = pd, size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(group = `sample-id`), position = pd, alpha = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'PuBuGn') +
  ggtitle('Number of reads after each DADA2 processing step') +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

rm(samples.to.exclude)
```

```{r}
dada_table <- read_delim("qiime/combined/2_Denoise_EE34_Pooled/table_dada2_exported/feature_table.tsv",
```

## Rarefaction curves

Rarefaction curves describe the number of observed species (here: sequence variants, ASVs) against the number of reads per sample. The curve is created by randomly re-sampling the pool of reads available for each sample and then plotting the average number of ASVs identified from the chosen reads. Generally, it initially grows rapidly and then slightly flattens (as the rarest species remain to be sampled).

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=8, fig.align='center'}
observed_rar <- read_csv("qiime/combined/5_Diversity/rarefaction_curves/observed_features.csv", 
                         show_col_types = FALSE)
observed_rar <- observed_rar %>%
  select(-batch) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -`sample-id`, 
                      names_to = 'depth_iter', 
                      values_to = 'asv_count',
                      values_drop_na = TRUE) %>%
  tidyr::separate(sep = '_', 
                  remove = TRUE, 
                  col = 'depth_iter', 
                  into = c('depth','iter')) %>%
  mutate(depth = as.numeric(gsub('depth\\-','',depth))) %>%
  group_by(`sample-id`, depth) %>%
  summarise(mean_asv_count = mean(asv_count), .groups = 'drop')

tmp_palette <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9,name = 'BrBG'))(n_distinct(observed_rar$`sample-id`))
ggplot(observed_rar, aes(x = depth, color = `sample-id`, y = mean_asv_count)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = tmp_palette) +
  theme_classic() +
  ggtitle('Rarefaction curves - ASV count') +
  xlab('Sequencing depth') +
  ylab('ASV count') +
  theme(legend.position = 'none') +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

rm(tmp_palette, observed_rar)
```

## Alpha-diversity

Alpha-diversity metrics measure the diversity of the microbial community (at the ASV level) within each sample. The following metrics were computed:  

- *Shannon diversity*: This index quantifies the uncertainty in predicting the species identity of an individual that is taken at random from the dataset. The higher the value, the higher the diversity of species is in the particular community. A value of 0 indicates a community that only has one species.  
- *Faith phylogenetic diversity*: This index also takes into account phylogenetic relatedness of species within a sample. See [here](https://danielpfaith.wordpress.com/phylogenetic-diversity/). Higher values indicate a larger spread over the phylogenetic tree, i.e. higher diversity.  

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=8, fig.align='center', message = FALSE}
faith_pd <- read_delim("qiime/combined/5_Diversity/faith_pd_vector_exported/alpha-diversity.tsv", 
                       delim = "\t", 
                       escape_double = FALSE, 
                       trim_ws = TRUE, 
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
shannon <- read_delim("qiime/combined/5_Diversity/shannon_vector_exported/alpha-diversity.tsv", 
                       delim = "\t", 
                       escape_double = FALSE, 
                       trim_ws = TRUE, 
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
alpha_div <- bind_rows(faith_pd %>% rename(sample = 1, val = 2) %>% mutate(metric = 'Faith PD'),
                       shannon %>% rename(sample = 1, val = 2) %>% mutate(metric = 'Shannon'))

ggplot(alpha_div, aes(x = val)) +
  geom_histogram(color = 'black', fill = 'darkolivegreen3', alpha = 0.6) +
  ggtitle('Distribution of alpha-diversity values') +
  xlab("Diversity value") +
  ylab("Number of samples") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Prinicipal coordinate analysis (PCoA)

We run PCoA with Bray-Curtis/ Weighted UniFrac distances to show an overview of samples and similarity between them. Samples from the same subject are connected with a line.


```{r}
get_pcoa <- function(df, n_dims){
  PCOA <- df %>% as.dist() %>% pcoa()
  eig_vals <- round(100* PCOA$values$Relative_eig[1:3],n_dims)
  pcoa_df <- PCOA$vectors[,1:n_dims] %>% as.data.frame() %>% tibble::rownames_to_column('sample')
  colnames(pcoa_df) <- gsub("Axis.", "axis_", colnames(pcoa_df))
  return(list(eig_vals, pcoa_df))
}

plot_pcoa<- function(ggdata, x_var, y_var,  eig_vals,metric, color_Var = "sample"){
  ggp <- ggplot(ggdata,aes_string(paste0("axis_", x_var), paste0("axis_", y_var), color = color_Var)) +
        geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) + 
        ggtitle(paste0('PCoA - ',metric,' (Axes ',x_var,' vs. ',y_var,')')) +
        xlab(paste0('Axis ',x_var,' (', eig_vals[x_var], '% variance explained)')) +
        ylab(paste0('Axis ',y_var,' (', eig_vals[y_var], '% variance explained)')) +
        theme_classic() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  return(ggp)
  
}
plot_pcoa_from_dist_mat <- function(dist_df, metric_name, axis_x = 1, axis_y = 2, color_Var = "sample", n_dims = 3, mdata = NULL) {
  pcoa_df <- get_pcoa(dist_df, n_dims)
  eig_vals <- pcoa_df[[1]]
  pcoa_df <- pcoa_df[[2]] 
  if (!is.null(mdata)){
    pcoa_df <- pcoa_df %>% left_join(mdata, by = 'sample')
  }
  ggp <- plot_pcoa(pcoa_df, axis_x, axis_y, eig_vals, metric_name, color_Var)

}
```

```{r}
format_sample_ids <- function(sample_vector){
  formatted_vector <- sample_vector %>% gsub("\\.","_",.)%>% gsub("-|\\.","_",.) %>% 
                      gsub("tasmul_|_[0-9].*","",.) %>% gsub("^X", "", .)

}
```

## Taxonomy assignment

To assign taxonomy per ASV we used qiime's `feature-classifier` plugin, with SILVA 138 as the reference database. Briefly, we first extracted reads corresponding to the below primers from the reference database, then we train a naive-bayes classifier (using `fit-classifier-naive-bayes`), and lastly we assigned a taxonomy to each ASV in our data using the trained model. The following non-default parameters were used in this process:   

| Parameter                       | Description                                         |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|`F_PRIMER=CCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG`     | Forward primer used to extract V3-V4 reads          |
|`R_PRIMER=GACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC`	| Reverse primer used to extract V3-V4 reads          |  
|`MIN_AMP_LEN=300`                | Remove extracted sequences shorter than this length |  
|`MAX_AMP_LEN=600`                | Remove extracted sequences longer than this length  |  

### Unassigned reads

Here we calculate the % of reads per sample for which taxonomy was not assigned, i.e. no match was found in the reference database. We expect these percentages to be low. 

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=5, fig.align='center'}
phy_relab <- read_delim("qiime/combined/6_Taxonomy_train_NB/taxa_phylum_table_compo_exported/feature-table.tsv", 
                        delim = "\t", escape_double = FALSE, 
                        trim_ws = TRUE, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)

tmp <- phy_relab %>%
  rename(otu = `#OTU ID`) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -otu, names_to = 'sample', values_to = 'relab') %>%
  filter(otu %in% c("d__Bacteria;__", "Unassigned;__")) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(relab_unassigned_perc = sum(relab), .groups = 'drop')

ggplot(tmp, aes(x = relab_unassigned_perc)) +
  geom_histogram(color = 'black', fill = 'cadetblue3', bins = 30) +
  ggtitle('Distribution of % of unassigned reads per sample') +
  ylab("Samples") +
  xlab("% of unassigned reads") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

Similarly, here we show the percent of reads succesfully assigned to each taxonomic rank. We note that 16S is considered inefficient in identifying bacteria at the species level or below.

```{r}
tax_assign <- read_delim("qiime/combined/6_Taxonomy_train_NB/taxonomy_classifications_exported/taxonomy.tsv", 
                         delim = "\t", escape_double = FALSE, 
                         trim_ws = TRUE, show_col_types = FALSE)
names(tax_assign) <- c('asv','full_taxonomy','confidence')

tax_assign <- tax_assign %>%
  tidyr::separate(col = full_taxonomy, into = c(NA,'p','c','o','f','g','s'), sep = '; ', fill = 'right') %>%
  # We apply some hard-coded rules to erase uninformative classifications
  mutate(s = ifelse(grepl('s__unidentified|s__uncultured|s__metagenome|s__human_gut|s__gut_metagenome|s__bacterium_enrichment|s__Bacteroidaceae_bacterium|s__.*_sp\\.|s__.*_bacterium', s),
                    NA, s)) %>%
  mutate(g = ifelse(grepl('g__uncultured', g), NA, g)) %>%
  mutate(f = ifelse(grepl('f__uncultured', f), NA, f)) %>%
  mutate(o = ifelse(grepl('o__uncultured', o), NA, o)) %>%
  mutate(c = ifelse(grepl('c__uncultured', c), NA, c)) 

get_asvs_with_rank <- function(tax_rank, tax_assign) {
  tax_assign %>%
    filter(!is.na(get({{tax_rank}}))) %>%
    pull(asv)
}

tmp <- dada_table %>% tibble::column_to_rownames('#OTU ID')
totals <- colSums(tmp)
tax_stats <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(level = '1-Phylum', perc = colSums(tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% get_asvs_with_rank('p', tax_assign),])*100 / totals),
  data.frame(level = '2-Class',  perc = colSums(tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% get_asvs_with_rank('c', tax_assign),])*100 / totals),
  data.frame(level = '3-Order',  perc = colSums(tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% get_asvs_with_rank('o', tax_assign),])*100 / totals),
  data.frame(level = '4-Family', perc = colSums(tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% get_asvs_with_rank('f', tax_assign),])*100 / totals),
  data.frame(level = '5-Genus',  perc = colSums(tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% get_asvs_with_rank('g', tax_assign),])*100 / totals),
  data.frame(level = '6-Species', perc = colSums(tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% get_asvs_with_rank('s', tax_assign),])*100 / totals)
)  
```

Each dot corresponds to a single sample.

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=5, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(tax_stats, 
       aes(x = level, y = perc, fill = level)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = 'black', width = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.4, size = 1, width = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'PuBuGn') +
  ggtitle('Percent of reads assigned to each taxonomic rank') +
  theme_classic() +
  ylab('Percent of reads') +
  xlab(NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```


### Phylum-level taxonomy barplots

Barplots below describe the phyla (or genera) identified in each sample. Rare taxa were grouped together (using a cutoff of mean relative abundance < 0.01) and are collectively named 'Others'. 

```{r}
# Recieves a compositional feature table and plots stacked barplots per sample 
plot_taxonomy <- function(relab_df, rare_otu_cutoff = 0.01, plot_title = 'Taxonomy barplots', legend_title = 'Taxon', n_legend_cols = 1) {
  relab_df <- relab_df %>%
    rename(otu = 1) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -otu, names_to = 'sample', values_to = 'relab') %>%
    # Re-normalize into relative abundance
    group_by(sample) %>%
    mutate(relab = relab / sum(relab)) %>%
    ungroup()
    
  # Group rare otu's together for plot simplicity
  rare_otus <- relab_df %>%
    group_by(otu) %>%
    summarise(mean_relab = mean(relab), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    filter(mean_relab < rare_otu_cutoff) %>%
    pull(otu)
  
  relab_df <- relab_df %>%
    mutate(otu_grouped = ifelse(otu %in% rare_otus, 'Others', otu)) %>%
    group_by(sample, otu_grouped) %>%
    summarise(relab = sum(relab), .groups = 'drop')

  tmp_palette <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9,name = 'RdYlGn'))(n_distinct(relab_df$otu_grouped))
  ggplot(relab_df, aes(fill = otu_grouped, y = relab, x = sample)) + 
    geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity", color = 'black') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = tmp_palette, name = legend_title) +
    theme_classic() +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
    ggtitle(plot_title) +
    xlab('Sample') +
    ylab('Relative abundance') +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = n_legend_cols)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 6, hjust = 1)) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 9)) +
    theme(legend.key.size = unit(9, "points"))
}
```

```{r fig.height=6, fig.width=10, fig.align='center'}
plot_taxonomy(phy_relab)
```

### Genus-level taxonomy barplots

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=10, fig.align='center'}
gns_relab <- read_delim("qiime/combined/6_Taxonomy_train_NB/taxa_genus_table_compo_exported/feature-table.tsv", 
    delim = "\t", escape_double = FALSE, 
    trim_ws = TRUE, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)

plot_taxonomy(gns_relab)
```

### Genera prevalence and abundance

Below are the distributions of genera prevalence (% of samples in which each genus was detected) and average abundance (the abundance of each genus is averaged over all samples). These histograms will aid in defining thresholds to discard 'rare genera'.  


```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=3, fig.align="center"}
tmp <- gns_relab %>% tibble::column_to_rownames(var = "#OTU ID")
genus_frequencies <- data.frame(genus_frequencies = rowSums(tmp > 0)/ncol(tmp))

ggplot(genus_frequencies, aes(x = genus_frequencies)) +
  geom_histogram(color = 'black', fill = 'cadetblue1', alpha = 0.6, bins = 50) +
  ggtitle('Distribution of genera prevalence') +
  xlab("Genus prevalence (% of samples)") +
  ylab("Number of genera") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) 

# Abundance
genus_avg_abun <- data.frame(genus_avg_abun = rowSums(tmp)/ncol(tmp))

ggplot(genus_avg_abun, aes(x = genus_avg_abun)) +
  geom_histogram(color = 'black', fill = 'cadetblue1', alpha = 0.6, bins = 100) +
  ggtitle('Distribution of genera average abundance') +
  xlab("Genus average abundance (% of reads)") +
  ylab("Number of genera") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) 
```
